title: Lithuanian customs confirms unauthorised access to its BAP user portal, partly restores services
date_note: Customs detected the activity on the evening of 10 November, per LRT/BNS published that night; no earlier day given.
summary: Lithuanian Customs detected signs of possible unlawful activity on the evening of 10 November and suspended its BAP user management portal (LRT/BNS). The Record reports the agency said its investigation confirmed unauthorised access and a potential breach affecting users who logged in on 9-10 November, and that it partly restored online services on 16 November. Chief Vygantas Paigozinas called it a targeted, sophisticated attack; no attacker is identified.
plain: Lithuania's customs agency shut a login portal after an intrusion it has now confirmed. Users who logged in on 9-10 November may be affected; some services are back.
exec: A national customs agency confirmed an intrusion into its login portal; services are partly restored and data theft is not established.
action: General advice: Lithuanian customs users who logged in on 9-10 November should watch for phishing that cites the incident.

validation.note: LRT (BNS, relaying the Customs Department's statement), The Record (quoting the agency and chief Vygantas Paigozinas) and ZATAZ are independent publishers; the agency's own confirmation of unauthorised access is relayed by The Record. The customs website itself was not read.

review.note: ZATAZ: detection 10 Nov, BAP suspended, unauthorised access confirmed, several hundred possibly affected, theft not established, no attacker named
